title: Blizzard QA-CWA: ratified AI and accommodation guardrails

observations.claim: CWA reported that Blizzard quality-assurance workers in Albany and Austin ratified a three-year union contract on 30 January 2026.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The public summary states that the contract contains enhanced regulations for AI and generative AI intended to support rather than replace or harm workers.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The same summary reports reasonable disability accommodations without discrimination or retaliation.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The contract also reports protections involving fair crediting, immigrant-worker discipline and seniority, and excessive overtime.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The bargaining units combined priorities across two locations, giving the contract a collective rather than individual complaint posture.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The full contract, covered-system definitions, enforcement procedures and named deployment outcomes are not public in the recovered source.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

findings.claim: A ratified collective agreement can join AI adoption, disability accommodation and discipline protections before a named adverse event occurs.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Public description of “enhanced regulations” does not authorize inference of a veto, threshold disclosure, audit right, or grievance remedy absent the clause text.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: The accommodation provision is a counterexample to treating disability-related variance as noncompliance by default, but its operation in an AI case is not publicly recovered.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: No named alert, discipline transaction, appeal, restoration or system revision has been recovered under the contract.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.
